chapter_seo_title: The Assassination: Li Huowang's Palace Rampage - Chapter 519
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang unleashes a full-scale assassination on the Imperial Palace, using shared pain as his weapon. But a new foe from the Ao-Jing Sect proves he’s not the only master of agony.
og_title: Palace of Blood: Li Huowang's Brutal Assassination Run
og_description: Li Huowang goes berserk in the Great Liang palace, using his own body as a weapon and a pain link to bring down the Empress Dowager and Eldest Princess.
twitter_description: The Ao-Jing Sect’s pain doctrine crashes into Li Huowang’s own. Who will break first?

lore_anchors.definition: A fictional sect in the novel fusing Zoroastrianism (袄教) and Nestorian Christianity (景教); they are masters of pain-based cultivation and the original owners of the Thousand Greats Record.
A brutal weapon made from the spine of a demon god; later used by Li Huowang as his primary armament in close-quarters combat.
A historical Chinese concealed weapon consisting of a weighted head connected to a rope or chain, used for entangling and bludgeoning.
A term for a foreign dancer from the Western Regions, often associated with Central Asian Sogdian culture, known for their sensual performances and allure in Tang dynasty literature.
